date.as_written: yāte sapty uḍupānale bhṛgudine nepālasamvatsare māse mādhavaśuklake raṣatithau ṛkṣe ca tiṣye ... samvat 317 vaiśākaśuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ | śukravāre | puṣyanakṣatre

notes: The verse date and the prose date agree. In the chronogram, sapti (7), uḍupa (1) and anala (3), read right to left, give NS 317. The verse also gives mādhava = Vaiśākha, rasa (written raṣa) = 6, bhṛgudina = Friday and tiṣya = Puṣya. NS 317 is about 1197 CE, so the king must be Lakṣmīkāmadeva II of the late 12th century, not Lakṣmīkāmadeva I of the 11th century. 'lakṣī' is an error for lakṣmī. 'jasa brahmaṇā' in the verse is probably a corruption of jayabrahmaṇā. 'lekhakapipra' stands for lekhaka-vipra. Both 'hastalikhāyitaṃ' and 'likhāyitaṃ' are causatives. Here they probably just mean 'written', because Jayabrahman calls himself lekhaka and the copy is for his own use. A commissioner role cannot be ruled out entirely, though. 'paṇḍitācāryaśrīśrī vaccharūdrācāryakṛtvā' is unclear: it may name a teacher, a reviser or the person who arranged the copy, and the name may be Vatsarudra. I have not checked the weekday against an ephemeris.
